Why 90% of Freelance Writers Quit—And How to Be the 10% Who Don’t

A practical look at the habits and business realities that drive freelancers out—and what makes a writing practice last.

  • By Paul Shannon
  • Original publication LinkedIn
  • Date June 5, 2025
  • Reading time 2 min
View original on LinkedIn ↗

About this work

This article reframes freelance attrition as an operating problem rather than a shortage of motivation. It considers the habits, expectations, business systems, and tolerance for uncertainty that determine whether writing work becomes repeatable.

From slogan to system

The familiar claim that most freelancers quit is useful only if the reasons are examined. The piece shifts attention from a dramatic percentage to the controllable work behind prospecting, delivery, revision, client communication, and persistence.

Experience-led commentary

Paul wrote from his own early freelance experience while keeping the article directed toward readers building their own practice. The value lies in translating hard-won working habits into concrete professional guidance.

Paul’s role

Paul developed and wrote the article independently from his experience operating PaulWrites.
